verdict.user:
A system read the meeting transcript below and extracted a list of tasks.
Evaluate the extraction against the ground truth.

MEETING TRANSCRIPT
------------------
Kim: Got two minutes? Two things before you disappear into meetings.

Ade: Go.

Kim: Staging is broken. The deploy job has been red since this morning, it can't pull the base image, looks like the registry token expired. Nobody can test anything until it's fixed.

Ade: That's mine, I rotated tokens yesterday and clearly missed the CI one. I'll regenerate the registry token, update the CI secret, and re-run the deploy. Give me an hour.

Kim: Second thing: Meridian. They asked for the updated proposal with the new pricing, and I promised it end of day today. The numbers are final in the spreadsheet, I just need you to drop them into the proposal doc and send it to their procurement contact, Lena, you have her email from the kickoff thread.

Ade: Updated proposal to Lena by end of day, numbers from the spreadsheet. Fine.

Kim: That's it. Go to your meetings.


GROUND TRUTH: EXPECTED TASKS
----------------------------
gt_01: Fix the broken staging deploy
  owner: Ade
  due: within the hour
  - deploy job red since morning: can't pull the base image, registry token expired during yesterday's rotation
  - regenerate the registry token, update the CI secret, re-run the deploy
  - blocks all testing until fixed
gt_02: Send Meridian the updated proposal
  owner: Ade
  due: end of day today
  - drop the final numbers from the spreadsheet into the proposal doc
  - send to Lena, Meridian's procurement contact (email in the kickoff thread)

ACCEPTABLE EXTRAS (count as neither hit nor hallucination)
(none)

FORBIDDEN (extracting any of these is an explicit error)
(none)

EXTRACTED TASKS (the system under test)
---------------------------------------
[0] Fix staging deploy job registry token authentication: Staging deploy job has been red since this morning and cannot pull base image due to expired registry token. Ade rotated tokens yesterday and missed the CI token.
Steps:
1. Regenerate the registry token for the CI service account / CI user.
2. Update the corresponding CI secret / environment variable with the new token.
3. Trigger a re-run of the staging deploy job.
4. Verify the job completes successfully.
Acceptance criteria:
- Deploy job status changes from red to green.
- Base image pulls successfully from registry.
- Staging environment is deployable and team can test. Estimated completion within 1 hour of start.
[1] Send updated Meridian proposal with new pricing to Lena: Meridian requested an updated proposal with new pricing, promised end of day today.
Steps:
1. Retrieve the final pricing numbers from the approved spreadsheet.
2. Open the Meridian proposal document and replace pricing sections with the numbers from the spreadsheet.
3. Retrieve Lena's email address from the Meridian kickoff thread; Lena is the procurement contact.
4. Send the updated proposal document to Lena by end of day today.
Acceptance criteria:
- Proposal document contains the final pricing numbers from the spreadsheet and no placeholders remain.
- Email sent to Lena with proposal attached/linked, sent on or before EOD today.
- Kim is notified once sent.

Instructions:
- Match extracted tasks to expected tasks SEMANTICALLY, on topic - names will
differ. An expected task may be matched by more than one extracted task
(that is a duplicate); an extracted task matches at most one expected task.
- For each expected task, judge each of its key points: covered means the
fact appears in the matched extracted task(s) name or description.
If an expected task has no match, no key point is covered.
- owner_mentioned / due_mentioned: does the matched extracted task text name
the listed owner / deadline? Use null when ground truth lists none.
- Classify every UNMATCHED extracted task: "acceptable" (matches an
acceptable-extra topic or is a reasonable, transcript-grounded extra),
"hallucination" (not grounded in the transcript), or "forbidden" (matches
a forbidden topic).

Answer with this exact JSON shape:
{
  "matches": [
    {"expected_id": "<id>", "extracted_indices": [<int>, ...],
      "key_points_covered": [true|false, ...],
      "owner_mentioned": true|false|null, "due_mentioned": true|false|null},
    ...one entry per expected task, in order...
  ],
  "extras": [
    {"extracted_index": <int>, "classification": "acceptable|hallucination|forbidden",
      "reason": "<short>"},
    ...one entry per unmatched extracted task...
  ],
  "safety_checks": [{"check": "<name>", "passed": true|false}, ...],
  "clarity": <1-5, 5 = every task name is crisp and each description is actionable>,
  "faithfulness": <1-5, 5 = no invented facts, owners, numbers, or deadlines>,
  "overall": <1-5, 5 = a team could work from this task list as-is>,
  "issues": ["<short issue>", ...]
}
"safety_checks" must contain one entry per listed safety check (empty list if none).
